name: Formal language
description: A precisely specified system of signs, assemblies (terms and relations), and syntactic rules for constructing well-formed expressions.

name: Quantifier (universal, existential)
description: The operators for-all and exists that bind a variable in a relation to express universal or existential properties.

name: Axiom scheme of substitution (logic)
description: The logical scheme permitting replacement of a free variable by a term in any well-formed relation, subject to no variable capture.

name: Modus ponens
description: The fundamental rule of inference: from A and A => B, deduce B.

name: Deductive system
description: The formal framework of proofs as finite sequences of relations, each an axiom or derived by rules of inference; a theorem is the final relation.

name: Hilbert epsilon operator (tau-operator)
description: A term-forming operator tau_x(R) selecting an object satisfying relation R if one exists, used to eliminate quantifiers and formalize choice at the logical level.

name: Axiom of the empty set
description: There exists a set having no elements, denoted empty-set.

name: Axiom of pairing
description: For any two objects a, b, there exists a set {a, b} whose only elements are a and b.

name: Axiom scheme of separation (comprehension)
description: For any set A and property P(x), there exists the set {x in A : P(x)} of exactly those elements of A satisfying P.

name: Axiom of union
description: For any set of sets F, there exists a set whose elements are exactly those belonging to at least one member of F.

name: Set membership (element-of relation)
description: The primitive binary relation x in A asserting that x is an element of the set A.

name: Subset (inclusion)
description: A subset-of B means every element of A is an element of B, defining the inclusion partial order on sets.

name: Set intersection
description: A cap B = {x : x in A and x in B}, the set of elements common to both A and B.

name: Set union (binary)
description: A cup B = {x : x in A or x in B}, the set of elements belonging to at least one of A, B.

name: Set complement (difference)
description: A \ B = {x in A : x not in B}, the set of elements in A but not in B.

name: Symmetric difference
description: A triangle B = (A \ B) u (B \ A), the set of elements belonging to exactly one of A, B.

name: Ordered pair
description: The object (a, b) defined via Kuratowski encoding such that (a,b) = (c,d) iff a = c and b = d.

name: Cartesian product
description: A x B = {(a, b) : a in A, b in B}, the set of all ordered pairs with first component in A and second in B.

name: Relation (graph of a relation)
description: A subset R of A x B; one writes xRy to mean (x, y) in R.

name: Function (map, mapping)
description: A relation f subset A x B such that for every a in A there exists exactly one b in B with (a, b) in f, written f : A -> B.

name: Injection (one-to-one map)
description: A function f : A -> B such that f(a1) = f(a2) implies a1 = a2.

name: Surjection (onto map)
description: A function f : A -> B such that for every b in B there exists a in A with f(a) = b.

name: Bijection
description: A function that is both injective and surjective, establishing a one-to-one correspondence.

name: Composition of functions
description: Given f : A -> B and g : B -> C, the composite g o f : A -> C defined by (g o f)(a) = g(f(a)).

name: Inverse function
description: For a bijection f : A -> B, the unique function f^{-1} : B -> A satisfying f^{-1} o f = id_A and f o f^{-1} = id_B.

name: Image and preimage
description: For f : A -> B, the direct image f(S) = {f(x) : x in S} and the inverse image f^{-1}(T) = {x in A : f(x) in T}.

name: Restriction and extension of a function
description: The restriction f|_S of f : A -> B to S subset A; an extension of g : S -> B is any f : A -> B with f|_S = g.

name: Family of sets (indexed family)
description: A function i -> A_i from an index set I to a collection of sets, written (A_i)_{i in I}.

name: Generalized union and intersection
description: For a family (A_i)_{i in I}, the union U_{i in I} A_i and intersection cap_{i in I} A_i, generalizing binary operations to arbitrary index sets.

name: Generalized Cartesian product (product of a family)
description: Product_{i in I} A_i, the set of all choice functions on the family, each selecting an element from A_i for every i.

name: Equivalence relation
description: A relation R on a set A that is reflexive, symmetric, and transitive.

name: Equivalence class
description: For an equivalence relation R on A, the class [a] = {x in A : xRa}.

name: Quotient set
description: A/R = {[a] : a in A}, the set of all equivalence classes, with canonical surjection pi : A -> A/R.

name: Canonical decomposition of a map
description: Every function f : A -> B factors uniquely as A -> A/~ -> f(A) -> B (surjection, bijection, inclusion).

name: Partition of a set
description: A family of pairwise disjoint nonempty subsets whose union is A, in canonical bijection with equivalence relations on A.

name: Diagonal of a product
description: Delta_A = {(a, a) : a in A} subset A x A, the graph of the identity function.

name: Projection map
description: The canonical surjections pr_1 : A x B -> A and pr_2 : A x B -> B extracting components of an ordered pair.

name: Preorder (quasi-order)
description: A reflexive and transitive relation, not necessarily antisymmetric; the quotient by the associated equivalence is a partial order.

name: Strict partial order
description: The irreflexive and transitive relation < derived from <= by x < y iff x <= y and x != y.

name: Greatest element and least element
description: In a poset, a greatest (resp. least) element a satisfies x <= a (resp. a <= x) for all x.

name: Supremum and infimum
description: sup S is the least upper bound of S; inf S is the greatest lower bound of S, when they exist.

name: Lattice
description: A poset in which every pair of elements has both a supremum (join) and an infimum (meet).

name: Complete lattice
description: A poset in which every subset has a supremum and an infimum.

name: Directed set
description: A nonempty preordered set in which every finite subset has an upper bound.

name: Increasing (order-preserving) map
description: A function f between posets such that x <= y implies f(x) <= f(y).

name: Order isomorphism
description: A bijection f between posets such that both f and f^{-1} are order-preserving.

name: Chain (totally ordered subset)
description: A subset of a poset that is totally ordered under the induced order.

name: Well-ordered set
description: A totally ordered set in which every nonempty subset has a least element.

name: Hausdorff maximality principle
description: Every partially ordered set contains a maximal chain; equivalent to axiom of choice.

name: Initial segment (section)
description: In a well-ordered set W, the set S_a = {x in W : x < a} of all elements strictly preceding a.

name: Comparability of well-ordered sets
description: Any two well-ordered sets are comparable: one is order-isomorphic to an initial segment of the other.

name: Cantor's theorem
description: For any set A, there is no surjection from A onto P(A); equivalently |A| < |P(A)|.

name: Equipotence (equinumerosity)
description: Two sets are equipotent if there exists a bijection between them.

name: Finite set
description: A set equipotent to some natural number {0, 1, ..., n-1}.

name: Countable set (denumerable)
description: A set equipotent to a subset of the natural numbers; countably infinite if equipotent to N.

name: Disjoint union (coproduct of sets)
description: A disjoint-union B = (A x {0}) u (B x {1}), a union keeping copies distinct even when they overlap.

name: Absorption law for infinite cardinals
description: For an infinite cardinal kappa, kappa + kappa = kappa * kappa = kappa.

name: Mathematical induction
description: If P(0) holds and P(n) => P(n+1), then P(n) holds for all natural numbers n.

name: Arithmetic of natural numbers
description: Addition and multiplication on N defined by recursion, satisfying commutativity, associativity, distributivity.

name: Order on natural numbers
description: The total order on N where m <= n iff m subset n (as sets), making (N, <=) a well-ordered set.

name: Species of structures
description: Bourbaki's formal specification: base sets, auxiliary sets, typification via echelon construction, and an axiom invariant under transport.

name: Echelon construction type
description: A set obtained from base sets by iterated application of power set and Cartesian product, providing the type of a structure.

name: Isomorphism of structures
description: A bijection between base sets of two structures of the same species that transports one structure to the other.

name: Transport of structures
description: Transferring a structure from one set to another via a bijection, preserving all structural axioms.
function_signature: (Structure on A, Bijection A -> B) -> Structure on B

name: Induced structure (substructure)
description: The structure inherited by a subset of the base set, obtained by restricting the structural data.

name: Product structure
description: The structure on a Cartesian product obtained by combining the structures on each factor componentwise.

name: Quotient structure
description: The structure induced on a quotient set A/R when the equivalence relation R is compatible with the given structure.

name: Initial structure
description: The coarsest structure on a set making a given family of maps into structured sets into morphisms.

name: Final structure
description: The finest structure on a set making a given family of maps from structured sets into morphisms.

name: Morphism (of a species of structures)
description: A map between base sets that respects the structural data; the precise definition depends on the species.

name: Neighborhood filter
description: The filter V(x) of all neighborhoods of a point x in a topological space, whose properties characterize the topology.

name: Filter
description: A nonempty collection of subsets of a set X, closed under finite intersection and supersets, and not containing the empty set.

name: Filter base (basis of a filter)
description: A nonempty collection of nonempty subsets such that any two members contain a common refinement; it generates a filter.

name: Convergence of a filter
description: A filter F on a topological space converges to x if F is finer than the neighborhood filter of x, i.e., V(x) subset F.

name: Cluster point of a filter
description: A point x such that every neighborhood of x meets every set in the filter.

name: Continuous map
description: A function f : X -> Y between topological spaces such that the preimage of every open set in Y is open in X.

name: Open map and closed map
description: A map sending open (resp. closed) sets to open (resp. closed) sets.

name: Subspace topology (induced topology)
description: The topology on a subset A of X whose open sets are intersections of open sets of X with A.

name: Initial topology
description: The coarsest topology on X making a given family of maps f_i : X -> Y_i continuous, with subbase {f_i^{-1}(U_i)}.

name: Final topology
description: The finest topology on Y making a given family of maps g_i : X_i -> Y continuous.

name: Hausdorff space (T2)
description: A topological space in which any two distinct points have disjoint neighborhoods.

name: T1 space
description: A topological space in which every singleton {x} is closed.

name: Regular space (T3)
description: A T1 space in which each point and disjoint closed set can be separated by disjoint open sets.

name: Completely regular space (Tychonoff, T3.5)
description: A T1 space in which points and disjoint closed sets can be separated by continuous real-valued functions.

name: Limit of a function
description: f(x) -> l as x -> a along a filter means the image filter converges to l, unifying all notions of limit.

name: Net (Moore-Smith sequence)
description: A function from a directed set into a topological space, generalizing sequences.

name: Connected space
description: A topological space that cannot be expressed as the union of two disjoint nonempty open sets.

name: Connected component
description: The maximal connected subset containing a given point; connected components partition the space into closed sets.

name: Locally connected space
description: A space in which every point has a neighborhood base consisting of connected open sets.

name: Second-countable space
description: A topological space possessing a countable base for its topology.

name: First-countable space
description: A topological space in which every point has a countable neighborhood base.

name: Separable space
description: A topological space containing a countable dense subset.

name: Uniform space (uniformity)
description: A set X equipped with a filter on X x X (entourages) containing the diagonal, symmetric, and satisfying the triangle condition.

name: Entourage (surrounding)
description: A member V of the uniformity; V[x] = {y : (x,y) in V} is the V-neighborhood of x.

name: Uniform topology
description: The topology on a uniform space where U is open iff for each x in U there exists entourage V with V[x] subset U.

name: Uniformly continuous map
description: A function f between uniform spaces such that for every entourage W of Y, (f x f)^{-1}(W) is an entourage of X.

name: Cauchy filter
description: A filter on a uniform space such that for every entourage V, there exists F in the filter with F x F subset V.

name: Complete uniform space
description: A uniform space in which every Cauchy filter converges.

name: Completion of a uniform space
description: A complete Hausdorff uniform space X-hat with uniformly continuous dense embedding X -> X-hat, unique up to uniform isomorphism.

name: Uniform isomorphism
description: A bijection f between uniform spaces such that both f and f^{-1} are uniformly continuous.

name: Product uniformity
description: The coarsest uniformity on the product making all projections uniformly continuous.

name: Induced uniformity (subspace uniformity)
description: The uniformity on a subset A induced by restricting entourages to A x A.

name: Minimal Cauchy filter
description: A Cauchy filter minimal among all Cauchy filters, used in the construction of completions.

name: Left uniform structure on a topological group
description: The uniformity on G with entourage base {(x,y) : x^{-1}y in V} where V ranges over identity neighborhoods.

name: Subgroup topology
description: The subspace topology on a subgroup H of a topological group G, making H a topological group.

name: Quotient group topology
description: The quotient topology on G/H for a normal subgroup H, making G/H a topological group and projection open.

name: Closure of a subgroup
description: The closure of a subgroup in a topological group is again a subgroup; the closure of a normal subgroup is normal.

name: Neighborhood base at the identity
description: A topological group's topology is completely determined by a neighborhood base at identity e, since translation is a homeomorphism.

name: Open subgroup theorem
description: Every open subgroup of a topological group is also closed; every subgroup containing an open subgroup is open.

name: Completion of a topological group
description: The Hausdorff completion of a topological group carries a canonical topological group structure.

name: Completeness of R (least upper bound property)
description: Every nonempty subset of R bounded above has a least upper bound (supremum) in R.

name: Archimedean property
description: For any real x > 0 and y, there exists natural n with nx > y; equivalently, Z is unbounded in R.

name: Density of Q in R
description: Between any two distinct real numbers there exists a rational number; Q is dense in R.

name: Order topology on R
description: The topology on R generated by open intervals (a, b), coinciding with the metric topology from |x - y|.

name: Extended real line
description: R-bar = R u {-inf, +inf}, a compact totally ordered space extending R with two points at infinity.

name: Absolute value (on R)
description: The function |x| = max(x, -x) on R, defining the standard metric d(x,y) = |x - y|.

name: Monotone convergence for sequences in R
description: Every bounded monotone sequence in R converges to its supremum (if increasing) or infimum (if decreasing).

name: Right and left limits
description: For a real function, f(a+) = lim_{x->a, x>a} f(x) and f(a-) = lim_{x->a, x<a} f(x).

name: Power function
description: x^alpha = exp(alpha ln x) for x > 0, extending integer powers to arbitrary real exponents.

name: Euclidean topology on R^n
description: The product topology on R^n, equivalently the metric topology from the Euclidean norm.

name: Normed vector space (over R)
description: A real vector space equipped with a norm satisfying positive definiteness, homogeneity, and the triangle inequality.

name: Metric uniformity
description: The uniformity on a metric space with entourage base {(x,y) : d(x,y) < epsilon} for epsilon > 0.

name: Equivalent norms on finite-dimensional spaces
description: On a finite-dimensional real vector space, all norms are equivalent, inducing the same topology.

name: Projective limit (inverse limit)
description: For a directed inverse system with connecting morphisms, the subspace of the product consisting of compatible threads.

name: Inductive limit (direct limit)
description: For a directed system with connecting morphisms, the quotient of the disjoint union identifying elements related by morphisms.

name: Solenoid
description: The projective limit of the inverse system ... -> S^1 ->^{xn} S^1, a compact connected abelian group not locally connected.

name: Profinite group
description: A topological group that is a projective limit of finite discrete groups; equivalently, compact totally disconnected Hausdorff.

name: Quasi-compact space
description: A topological space (not necessarily Hausdorff) in which every open cover has a finite subcover; Bourbaki reserves 'compact' for Hausdorff.

name: Finite intersection property characterization of compactness
description: A space is compact iff every collection of closed sets with the finite intersection property has nonempty intersection.

name: Continuous image of compact is compact
description: The continuous image of a compact space is compact.

name: Closed subsets of compact spaces are compact
description: Every closed subset of a compact space is compact; every compact subset of a Hausdorff space is closed.

name: Compact Hausdorff implies normal
description: Every compact Hausdorff space is normal (T4).

name: Continuous bijection from compact to Hausdorff is homeomorphism
description: A continuous bijection from a compact space to a Hausdorff space is automatically a homeomorphism.

name: Proper map
description: A continuous map f : X -> Y such that preimages of compact sets are compact (equivalently, f x id_Z is closed for every Z).

name: Locally finite family
description: A family of subsets such that every point has a neighborhood meeting only finitely many members.

name: Refinement of a cover
description: A cover {V_j} refines {U_i} if every V_j is contained in some U_i.

name: Paracompactness of metrizable spaces (Stone's theorem)
description: Every metrizable space is paracompact; every open cover has a sigma-discrete open refinement.

name: Nowhere dense set
description: A set whose closure has empty interior.

name: Meager set (first category)
description: A countable union of nowhere dense sets; by Baire's theorem, a complete metric space is not meager in itself.

name: Characterization of semicontinuity via liminf/limsup
description: f is lower semicontinuous at x iff f(x) <= lim inf_{y->x} f(y); upper iff f(x) >= lim sup_{y->x} f(y).

name: Supremum of lower semicontinuous functions
description: The pointwise supremum of any family of lower semicontinuous functions is lower semicontinuous.

name: Paracompactness and partitions of unity
description: A Hausdorff space is paracompact iff every open cover admits a subordinate partition of unity.

name: Lindelof space
description: A topological space in which every open cover has a countable subcover.

name: Second-countable implies Lindelof
description: Every second-countable space is Lindelof, separable, and hereditarily Lindelof.

name: Compact-open topology
description: The topology on C(X,Y) generated by subbasic sets {f : f(K) subset U} where K compact and U open.

name: Topology of uniform convergence
description: The topology on function spaces defined by the uniformity: f and g are V-close if (f(x),g(x)) in V for all x.

name: Topology of compact convergence
description: The topology on C(X,Y) defined by uniform convergence on each compact subset of X.

name: Pointwise convergence topology
description: The topology on Y^X induced by the product topology; convergence means convergence at each point.

name: Evaluation map
description: The map ev : C(X,Y) x X -> Y defined by ev(f,x) = f(x); continuous when C(X,Y) has the compact-open topology and X is locally compact.

name: Exponential law for function spaces
description: For locally compact Hausdorff X, C(X x Y, Z) -> C(Y, C(X,Z)) by currying is a homeomorphism under compact-open topology.

name: Uniform limit of continuous functions is continuous
description: C(X,Y) is closed in Y^X under the topology of uniform convergence when Y is Hausdorff.

name: Completeness of function spaces
description: If Y is a complete uniform space, the space of bounded uniformly continuous functions X -> Y is complete under uniform convergence.

name: Filter generated by a base
description: The unique smallest filter containing a given filter base, consisting of all supersets of members of the base.

name: Finer and coarser topologies
description: Topology T1 is finer than T2 if T2 subset T1; the identity (X,T1) -> (X,T2) is then continuous.

name: Discrete and indiscrete topologies
description: The finest topology (every subset open) and the coarsest topology ({empty, X} only) on a set X.

name: Clopen set
description: A set that is simultaneously open and closed; a space is connected iff its only clopen sets are empty and X.

name: Sigma-compact space
description: A topological space that is a countable union of compact subsets.

name: Cauchy sequence
description: A sequence (x_n) in a metric/uniform space such that for every entourage V, there exists N with (x_m, x_n) in V for all m, n >= N.

name: Pseudometric uniformity
description: A pseudometric (allowing d(x,y)=0 for x != y) generates a uniformity; the associated topology need not be Hausdorff.

name: Continuity via filters
description: A map f : X -> Y is continuous at x iff the image filter of the neighborhood filter of x converges to f(x).

name: Universal property of completion
description: Every uniformly continuous map from X to a complete Hausdorff uniform space extends uniquely through X -> X-hat.

name: Compactness equals complete and totally bounded
description: A uniform space is compact iff it is complete and totally bounded.

name: Lebesgue covering lemma
description: For every open cover of a compact metric space, there exists delta > 0 such that every subset of diameter < delta lies in some member.

name: Topological embedding
description: An injective continuous map f : X -> Y that is a homeomorphism onto its image f(X) with the subspace topology.

name: Monoid
description: A set equipped with an associative binary operation possessing an identity element.

name: Group
description: A monoid in which every element is invertible.

name: Characteristic of a ring
description: The nonnegative generator of the kernel of the unique ring homomorphism Z -> A.

name: Opposite ring
description: For a ring A, the ring A^op with the same additive group but reversed multiplication a *' b = ba.

name: Left module / right module
description: A module where scalars act on the left (resp. right), with axiom (ab)x = a(bx) for left modules and x(ab) = (xa)b for right modules.

name: Basis of a module
description: A family of elements such that every element of the module can be written uniquely as a finite linear combination of them.

name: Rank of a linear map
description: The dimension of the image of a linear map between vector spaces.

name: Direct sum decomposition
description: A module M is a direct sum of submodules M_1,...,M_n if the canonical map M_1 + ... + M_n -> M is an isomorphism.

name: Noetherian module
description: A module satisfying the ascending chain condition on submodules, equivalently every submodule is finitely generated.

name: Artinian module
description: A module satisfying the descending chain condition on submodules.

name: Annihilator
description: For a submodule N of M, the ideal Ann(N) = {a in A : aN = 0}; dually for an ideal I, Ann_M(I) = {x in M : Ix = 0}.

name: Multilinear map
description: A map f: M_1 x ... x M_n -> N that is linear in each variable when the others are held fixed.

name: Right exactness of tensor product
description: The functor M tensor_A (-) is right exact: it preserves cokernels and direct sums but not injections in general.

name: Tensor algebra
description: The graded algebra T(M) = direct_sum_{n>=0} M^{tensor n} with concatenation multiplication, universal for linear maps from M to associative algebras.

name: Exterior product (wedge product)
description: The product in the exterior algebra, denoted x wedge y, satisfying x wedge x = 0 and x wedge y = -y wedge x.

name: Exterior power
description: The p-th component Lambda^p(M) of the exterior algebra, the quotient of M^{tensor p} by tensors with a repeated factor.

name: Symmetric algebra
description: The quotient S(M) = T(M)/<x tensor y - y tensor x>, a graded commutative algebra universal for linear maps from M to commutative algebras.

name: Symmetric power
description: The p-th component S^p(M) of the symmetric algebra, the quotient of M^{tensor p} by differences of permuted tensors.

name: Graded algebra
description: An algebra A with a direct sum decomposition A = direct_sum_{n>=0} A_n such that A_m * A_n subset A_{m+n}.

name: Extension of scalars
function_signature: (A-module M, ring hom A -> B) -> B-module M tensor_A B
description: Constructs a B-module from an A-module M and a ring homomorphism A -> B via the tensor product M tensor_A B.

name: Polynomial ring in several variables
description: The ring A[X_1,...,X_n] defined inductively as A[X_1,...,X_{n-1}][X_n], or as formal sums over multi-indices.

name: Euclidean division for polynomials
description: For f, g in K[X] with g nonzero and K a field, there exist unique q, r with f = qg + r and deg(r) < deg(g).

name: Root of a polynomial
description: An element alpha in an extension of the coefficient ring such that f(alpha) = 0.

name: Factor theorem
description: An element alpha is a root of f in K[X] if and only if (X - alpha) divides f.

name: Irreducible polynomial
description: A nonconstant polynomial that cannot be written as a product of two polynomials of lower degree.

name: Unique factorization in K[X]
description: The polynomial ring K[X] over a field K is a UFD: every nonconstant polynomial factors uniquely into irreducibles up to units.

name: Greatest common divisor of polynomials
description: The monic polynomial of greatest degree dividing two given polynomials, computable by the Euclidean algorithm.

name: Partial fraction decomposition
function_signature: (rational fraction in K(X)) -> polynomial + sum of a_ij/(X - alpha_i)^j
description: Expresses a rational fraction as a polynomial plus a sum of terms with prime-power denominators via the Chinese remainder theorem.

name: Algebraic element
description: An element alpha in L that is a root of some nonzero polynomial in K[X].

name: Transcendental element
description: An element alpha in L that is not algebraic over K.

name: Simple algebraic extension
description: An extension K(alpha)/K generated by a single algebraic element alpha, isomorphic to K[X]/(minimal polynomial of alpha).

name: Tower law (multiplicativity of degrees)
description: If K subset L subset M are field extensions, then [M:K] = [M:L]*[L:K].

name: Existence and uniqueness of algebraic closure
description: Every field admits an algebraic closure, and any two algebraic closures are isomorphic (though not canonically).

name: Separable polynomial
description: A polynomial whose roots in an algebraic closure are all distinct, equivalently gcd(f, f') = 1.

name: Inseparable extension / purely inseparable extension
description: An algebraic extension that is not separable; purely inseparable if every element has minimal polynomial X^{p^n} - a in characteristic p.

name: Perfect field
description: A field of characteristic 0, or of characteristic p in which the Frobenius endomorphism x -> x^p is surjective.

name: Normal extension
description: An algebraic extension L/K such that every irreducible polynomial in K[X] with a root in L splits completely in L.

name: Transcendence basis
description: A maximal algebraically independent subset of L over K, such that L is algebraic over K(B).

name: Norm and trace of a field extension
description: For a finite extension L/K and alpha in L, N_{L/K}(alpha) = det(mult. by alpha) and Tr_{L/K}(alpha) = trace(mult. by alpha) as K-linear endomorphisms.

name: Artin's theorem on characters
description: Distinct characters (homomorphisms) from a group to the multiplicative group of a field are linearly independent over that field.

name: Totally ordered group
description: A group equipped with a total order compatible with the group operation: x <= y implies xz <= yz and zx <= zy.

name: Archimedean ordered group
description: A totally ordered group in which for any positive a, b there exists n in Z with na > b, equivalently embeddable in (R,+).

name: Valuation (Krull valuation)
description: A map v: K* -> Gamma to a totally ordered abelian group satisfying v(xy) = v(x) + v(y) and v(x+y) >= min(v(x),v(y)).

name: Absolute value on a field
description: A map |*|: K -> R_{>=0} satisfying |x| = 0 iff x = 0, |xy| = |x||y|, and |x+y| <= |x|+|y|.

name: Convex subgroup
description: A subgroup H of a totally ordered group G such that if a <= x <= b with a,b in H then x in H.

name: Elementary divisors
description: The prime power factors in the primary decomposition of a finitely generated module over a PID, determining its isomorphism class.

name: Characteristic polynomial
description: For a matrix A or endomorphism u, the polynomial chi(X) = det(XI - A) whose roots are the eigenvalues with algebraic multiplicities.

name: Minimal polynomial of an endomorphism
description: The monic generator of the annihilator ideal of the K[X]-module defined by the endomorphism, dividing the characteristic polynomial.

name: Torsion submodule
description: For a module M over an integral domain A, the submodule Tors(M) = {m in M : am = 0 for some nonzero a in A}.

name: Torsion-free module
description: A module M over an integral domain such that Tors(M) = 0, i.e., am = 0 with a nonzero implies m = 0.

name: Semisimple module
description: A module that is a direct sum of simple modules, equivalently every submodule is a direct summand.

name: Semisimple ring
description: A ring that is semisimple as a module over itself, equivalently an Artinian ring with zero Jacobson radical.

name: Simple ring
description: A ring with no two-sided ideals other than 0 and itself (and with R^2 nonzero).

name: Symmetric bilinear form
description: A bilinear form Phi with Phi(x,y) = Phi(y,x) for all x,y.

name: Alternating bilinear form
description: A bilinear form Phi with Phi(x,x) = 0 for all x, hence Phi(x,y) = -Phi(y,x).

name: Sesquilinear form
description: A map Phi: M x M -> K that is linear in one variable and conjugate-linear with respect to an involution in the other.

name: Hermitian form
description: A sesquilinear form Phi satisfying Phi(y,x) = sigma(Phi(x,y)) where sigma is the given involution.

name: Non-degenerate form
description: A bilinear or quadratic form for which the canonical map M -> M* is injective, equivalently the radical is zero.

name: Radical of a form
description: The submodule rad(Phi) = {x in M : Phi(x,y) = 0 for all y in M}, the kernel of the map M -> M* induced by the form.

name: Orthogonal complement
description: For a subset S of M with bilinear form, the submodule S^perp = {y in M : Phi(x,y) = 0 for all x in S}.

name: Witt's theorem
description: An isometry between non-degenerate subspaces of a regular quadratic space extends to an isometry of the whole space.

name: Witt group
description: The group W(K) of isometry classes of non-degenerate quadratic forms over K modulo hyperbolic forms, with orthogonal sum.

name: Hyperbolic plane (quadratic forms)
description: A non-degenerate quadratic module of dimension 2 with basis {e,f} satisfying q(e) = q(f) = 0 and Phi(e,f) = 1.

name: Symplectic group
description: The group Sp(M,Phi) of linear maps preserving a non-degenerate alternating bilinear form.

name: Spin group
description: The double cover Spin(n) of SO(n) constructed inside the even part of the Clifford algebra, kernel of the spinor norm on the special Clifford group.

name: Spinor norm
description: A homomorphism from the orthogonal group to K*/K*^2 defined via the Clifford algebra, measuring the signed length of reflections composing an isometry.

name: Associative algebra
description: A ring A that is also a module over a commutative ring K, with K acting centrally: k(ab) = (ka)b = a(kb).

name: Lie subalgebra
description: A submodule of a Lie algebra closed under the Lie bracket.

name: Ideal of a Lie algebra
description: A Lie subalgebra h of g such that [g,h] subset h.

name: Commutator Lie algebra
description: For an associative algebra A, the Lie algebra A^- with bracket [a,b] = ab - ba.

name: Poincare-Birkhoff-Witt theorem
description: The canonical map g -> U(g) is injective, and ordered monomials of a basis form a basis of the universal enveloping algebra.

name: Free Lie algebra
description: The Lie algebra L(X) on a set X satisfying the universal property that every map X -> g extends uniquely to a homomorphism L(X) -> g.

name: Nilpotent Lie algebra
description: A Lie algebra whose lower central series g supset [g,g] supset [g,[g,g]] supset ... terminates at 0 in finitely many steps.

name: Solvable Lie algebra
description: A Lie algebra whose derived series g supset [g,g] supset [[g,g],[g,g]] supset ... terminates at 0 in finitely many steps.

name: Abelian Lie algebra
description: A Lie algebra in which [x,y] = 0 for all x,y.

name: Faithfully flat module
description: A flat A-module M such that M tensor_A N = 0 implies N = 0, equivalently M tensor_A (-) reflects exactness.

name: Faithfully flat descent
function_signature: (Module or algebra over A, faithfully flat A -> B) -> descended properties over A
description: Deduces properties of modules or algebras over A from their base change to a faithfully flat extension B.

name: Local-global principle
function_signature: (Property of module M) -> (Property holds iff it holds at all localizations M_p)
description: A property of modules holds globally iff it holds after localization at every prime ideal.

name: Support of a module
description: The set Supp(M) = {p in Spec(A) : M_p nonzero}, a closed subset of Spec(A) when M is finitely generated.

name: Associated graded ring/module
description: For a filtered ring A, the graded ring gr(A) = direct_sum_n A_n/A_{n+1}, capturing the leading term structure.

name: Filtered ring
description: A ring equipped with a decreasing sequence of ideals ... supset F_n supset F_{n+1} supset ... compatible with multiplication: F_m * F_n subset F_{m+n}.

name: I-adic filtration
description: The filtration of a ring A by powers of an ideal I: F_n = I^n.

name: I-adic topology
description: The linear topology on a ring or module defined by powers of an ideal I, where {I^n} forms a neighborhood base of 0.

name: Hilbert function / Hilbert-Samuel function
description: For a graded module M, H(n) = dim_k(M_n); for I-adic filtrations, H_I(n) = length(M/I^{n+1}M), both eventually polynomial.

name: Primary ideal
description: An ideal q such that if ab in q and a not in q then b^n in q for some n, equivalently A/q has every zero-divisor nilpotent.

name: Uniqueness theorems for primary decomposition
description: The associated primes and primary components for minimal primes are uniquely determined; embedded components may not be unique.

name: Integral element
description: An element b of a ring extension B supset A is integral over A if it satisfies a monic polynomial with coefficients in A.

name: Lying-over theorem
description: If A subset B is an integral extension, then for every prime ideal p of A there exists a prime ideal q of B with q intersect A = p.

name: Valuation ring
description: An integral domain A such that for every nonzero element x of its fraction field, either x in A or x^{-1} in A.

name: Place
description: An equivalence class of valuations on a field, or a homomorphism from a valuation ring to a field together with infinity.

name: Uniformizer
description: A generator of the maximal ideal of a DVR, equivalently an element of valuation 1.

name: Rank of a valuation
description: The Krull dimension of the associated valuation ring, equivalently the order type of convex subgroups of the value group.

name: Henselian ring
description: A local ring satisfying the conclusion of Hensel's lemma, equivalently every finite algebra over it is a product of local algebras.

name: Ramification index and residue degree
description: For a valued field extension L/K, e = [v(L*):v(K*)] and f = [kappa_L:kappa_K]; the fundamental inequality gives ef <= [L:K].

name: Extension of valuations
description: Every valuation on a field K extends to any algebraic extension L of K, with at most [L:K] extensions.

name: Principal divisor
description: The divisor div(f) associated to a nonzero element f of the fraction field, defined as sum_v v(f)*[v] over height-1 primes.

name: Factorial ring (UFD)
description: An integral domain with unique factorization into irreducibles; equivalently a Noetherian integrally closed domain with trivial divisor class group.

name: Invertible ideal
description: A fractional ideal I such that I*I^{-1} = A where I^{-1} = {x in K : xI subset A}; equivalently a locally principal fractional ideal.

name: Unique factorization of ideals in Dedekind domains
description: In a Dedekind domain, every nonzero ideal factors uniquely as a product of prime ideals.

name: Approximation theorem for valuations
description: Given finitely many independent valuations and target elements, one can find x simultaneously approximating each target.

name: System of parameters
description: In a Noetherian local ring of dimension d, a sequence of d elements whose generated ideal is m-primary.

name: Dimension theorem for Noetherian local rings
description: The Krull dimension equals the degree of the Hilbert-Samuel polynomial, equals the minimum number of generators of an m-primary ideal.

name: Dimension of polynomial rings
description: If A is a Noetherian ring, then dim(A[X]) = dim(A) + 1.

name: Catenary ring
description: A Noetherian ring in which all maximal chains of primes between any pair p subset q have the same length.

name: Universally catenary ring
description: A Noetherian ring A such that every finitely generated A-algebra is catenary.

name: Unmixedness theorem
description: In a Cohen-Macaulay ring, every ideal generated by height-many elements is unmixed (all associated primes are minimal of equal height).

name: Multiplicity of a local ring
description: The normalized leading coefficient of the Hilbert-Samuel polynomial, measuring algebraic multiplicity; equals 1 for regular local rings.

name: Coefficient field / coefficient ring
description: A subfield or complete DVR of a complete local ring mapping isomorphically to the residue field, guaranteed by the Cohen structure theorem.

name: Weierstrass division theorem
description: Division with remainder by a Weierstrass polynomial in k[[X_1,...,X_n]]: unique q and r with deg_{X_n}(r) < d.

name: Nagata ring (Japanese ring)
description: A Noetherian domain whose integral closure in any finite extension of its fraction field is a finite module.

name: Excellent ring
description: A universally catenary Noetherian ring with geometrically regular formal fibers and open regular locus; complete local rings are excellent.

name: Depth
description: The length of a maximal regular sequence in m on a finitely generated module over a Noetherian local ring, equivalently the smallest i with Ext^i(k,M) nonzero.

name: Regular sequence
description: A sequence x_1,...,x_n such that x_i is a non-zero-divisor on M/(x_1,...,x_{i-1})M for each i, and the quotient is nonzero.

name: Depth lemma
description: For a short exact sequence 0 -> M' -> M -> M'' -> 0, depth(M) >= min(depth(M'), depth(M'') + 1).

name: Injective hull (injective envelope)
description: The minimal injective module containing M as an essential submodule, unique up to isomorphism.

name: Matlis duality
description: Over a complete Noetherian local ring, Hom(-,E(k)) gives an anti-equivalence between finitely generated and Artinian modules.

name: Dualizing module (canonical module)
description: A finitely generated module over a Cohen-Macaulay local ring satisfying local duality via Ext and local cohomology.

name: Local duality theorem
description: For a complete Noetherian local ring of dimension d with dualizing module omega, H^i_m(M)^v isomorphic to Ext^{d-i}(M, omega).

name: Regular rings have finite global dimension
description: A Noetherian local ring is regular iff it has finite global dimension, and then gl.dim(A) = dim(A).

name: Bass's theorem
description: A Noetherian local ring is Gorenstein iff it has finite injective dimension, and then inj.dim(A) = dim(A).

name: Derivative of a vector-valued function
description: For a function f mapping an interval of R into a normed vector space E, the derivative at a point x₀ is the limit of (f(x) - f(x₀))/(x - x₀) as x → x₀, when this limit exists in E.

name: Differentiability
description: A function f is differentiable at x₀ if there exists a continuous linear map L such that f(x₀ + h) = f(x₀) + L(h) + o(h) as h → 0.

name: Linearity of differentiation
description: The derivative operator is linear: (αf + βg)' = αf' + βg' for differentiable functions f, g and scalars α, β.

name: Product rule (Leibniz rule)
description: If f and g are differentiable real-valued functions, then (fg)' = f'g + fg'.

name: Chain rule
description: If g is differentiable at x₀ and f is differentiable at g(x₀), then f ∘ g is differentiable at x₀ with derivative f'(g(x₀)) · g'(x₀).

name: Derivative of the inverse function
description: If f is a continuous bijection differentiable at x₀ with f'(x₀) ≠ 0, then f⁻¹ is differentiable at f(x₀) with derivative 1/f'(x₀).

name: Monotonicity criterion via derivative
description: A differentiable function f on an interval is non-decreasing if and only if f'(x) ≥ 0 for all x in the interval.

name: Convexity criterion via second derivative
description: A twice-differentiable function f on an interval is convex if and only if f''(x) ≥ 0 for all x in the interval.

name: Higher-order derivative
description: The n-th derivative f⁽ⁿ⁾ is defined inductively as the derivative of f⁽ⁿ⁻¹⁾, when it exists.

name: Leibniz formula for n-th derivative of a product
description: The n-th derivative of a product fg equals Σₖ₌₀ⁿ C(n,k) f⁽ᵏ⁾g⁽ⁿ⁻ᵏ⁾.

name: Regulated function
description: A function f from an interval I into a Banach space E is regulated if it has a left limit and a right limit at every point of I, equivalently if it is a uniform limit of step functions.

name: Step function
description: A function on an interval that takes only finitely many values, each on a sub-interval of a finite partition.

name: Integral of a regulated function
description: The integral of a regulated function f is defined as the limit of integrals of step functions converging uniformly to f, and this limit is independent of the approximating sequence.

name: Primitive (antiderivative)
description: A primitive of a function f on an interval I is a function F such that F' = f on I.

name: Integration by parts
description: If f and g are continuously differentiable on [a,b], then ∫ₐᵇ f'(t)g(t) dt = f(b)g(b) - f(a)g(a) - ∫ₐᵇ f(t)g'(t) dt.

name: Change of variables in integrals
description: If φ is a C¹ diffeomorphism and f is regulated, then ∫_{φ(a)}^{φ(b)} f(t) dt = ∫ₐᵇ f(φ(u)) φ'(u) du.

name: Integral remainder for Taylor's formula
description: If f is of class Cⁿ⁺¹, the remainder in the n-th order Taylor expansion equals (1/n!) ∫₀ʰ (h-t)ⁿ f⁽ⁿ⁺¹⁾(x₀+t) dt.

name: Uniform convergence and integration
description: If a sequence of regulated functions converges uniformly to f, then f is regulated and the integral of the limit equals the limit of the integrals.

name: Improper integral (convergent integral on unbounded interval)
description: The integral ∫ₐ^∞ f(t) dt is defined as limₓ→∞ ∫ₐˣ f(t) dt when this limit exists.

name: Absolute convergence of improper integrals
description: If ∫ₐ^∞ ‖f(t)‖ dt converges, then ∫ₐ^∞ f(t) dt converges and ‖∫ₐ^∞ f(t) dt‖ ≤ ∫ₐ^∞ ‖f(t)‖ dt.

name: Power function x^α
description: For x > 0 and α ∈ R, defined as x^α = exp(α log x), extending integer powers to all real exponents.

name: Number π
description: Defined as twice the smallest positive zero of cosine, establishing the period 2π of the trigonometric functions.

name: Inverse trigonometric functions (arcsin, arccos, arctan)
description: The inverse functions of sin, cos, tan restricted to appropriate intervals where they are bijective, with derivatives 1/√(1-x²), -1/√(1-x²), 1/(1+x²) respectively.

name: Hyperbolic functions (sinh, cosh, tanh)
description: Defined as sinh(x) = (eˣ - e⁻ˣ)/2, cosh(x) = (eˣ + e⁻ˣ)/2, tanh(x) = sinh(x)/cosh(x), satisfying the identity cosh²(x) - sinh²(x) = 1.

name: Inverse hyperbolic functions
description: The inverses of sinh, cosh|[0,∞), tanh, expressible in terms of logarithm: arsinh(x) = log(x + √(x²+1)).

name: Analyticity of elementary functions
description: The functions exp, log, sin, cos, and their inverses are all real-analytic on their domains of definition, represented by convergent power series.

name: Growth comparison of elementary functions
description: As x → +∞, for any α > 0 and β > 0: (log x)^α = o(x^β) and x^β = o(e^{αx}), establishing the asymptotic hierarchy log ≪ polynomial ≪ exponential.

name: Lipschitz condition
description: A function f(t, y) satisfies a Lipschitz condition in y if ‖f(t, y₁) - f(t, y₂)‖ ≤ K‖y₁ - y₂‖ for some constant K and all (t, yᵢ) in the domain.

name: Integral equation formulation of ODE
description: The initial value problem y' = f(t,y), y(t₀) = y₀ is equivalent to the integral equation y(t) = y₀ + ∫_{t₀}^t f(s, y(s)) ds.

name: Maximal solution of an ODE
description: A solution defined on a maximal interval of existence that cannot be extended to a larger interval, whose existence is guaranteed by Zorn's lemma from local solutions.

name: Blow-up criterion (escape to boundary)
description: If the maximal interval of existence of a solution is bounded, then the solution leaves every compact subset of the domain of f, i.e., ‖y(t)‖ → ∞ or the solution approaches the boundary.

name: Linear ordinary differential equation
description: An ODE of the form y' = A(t)y + b(t), where A(t) is a continuous matrix-valued function and b(t) is continuous, whose solutions form an affine subspace.

name: Homogeneous linear ODE
description: A linear ODE of the form y' = A(t)y (with b = 0) whose solutions form a vector space of dimension equal to the order of the system.

name: Fundamental matrix (resolvent)
description: A matrix-valued function Φ(t) whose columns form a basis of solutions of y' = A(t)y, satisfying Φ' = A(t)Φ with Φ(t₀) = I.

name: Variation of constants (variation of parameters)
description: A method to solve the non-homogeneous equation y' = A(t)y + b(t) by writing y(t) = Φ(t)c(t) where Φ is the fundamental matrix, leading to c'(t) = Φ(t)⁻¹b(t).

name: Linear ODE with constant coefficients
description: The system y' = Ay with A constant has the explicit solution y(t) = e^{tA}y₀, reducible via Jordan normal form to exponential-polynomial expressions.

name: Differentiable dependence on parameters
description: If f(t, y, λ) is Cᵏ in all variables, then the solution y(t, λ) of y' = f(t, y, λ) is Cᵏ in the parameter λ.

name: Lagrange remainder
description: For f of class Cⁿ⁺¹, the remainder Rₙ(h) = f⁽ⁿ⁺¹⁾(x₀ + θh) hⁿ⁺¹/(n+1)! for some θ ∈ (0,1).

name: Asymptotic expansion
description: A formal series Σ aₙφₙ(x) is an asymptotic expansion of f(x) as x → x₀ if f(x) - Σₖ₌₀ⁿ aₖφₖ(x) = o(φₙ(x)) for each n, where (φₙ) is an asymptotic scale.

name: Asymptotic scale
description: A sequence of functions (φₙ) such that φₙ₊₁(x) = o(φₙ(x)) as x → x₀, providing a graded comparison framework for the growth or decay of functions.

name: Little-o and big-O notation
description: f = o(g) means f/g → 0 and f = O(g) means |f/g| is bounded, as x approaches a specified limit, providing a calculus of asymptotic comparison.

name: Asymptotic comparison of functions
description: The systematic use of asymptotic expansions and asymptotic scales to compare functions' growth rates, compute limits of indeterminate forms, and approximate functions near singular points.
function_signature: (Functions near a point) → (Asymptotic ordering and expansions)

name: Bernoulli numbers
description: The sequence of rational numbers Bₙ defined by the generating function t/(eᵗ - 1) = Σₙ₌₀^∞ Bₙ tⁿ/n!, with B₀ = 1, B₁ = -1/2, and B₂ₖ₊₁ = 0 for k ≥ 1.

name: Bernoulli polynomials
description: Polynomials Bₙ(x) defined by the generating function te^{xt}/(eᵗ - 1) = Σₙ₌₀^∞ Bₙ(x) tⁿ/n!, satisfying Bₙ'(x) = nBₙ₋₁(x) and Bₙ(0) = Bₙ.

name: Euler-Maclaurin summation formula
description: Relates a sum Σₖ₌ₐᵇ f(k) to the integral ∫ₐᵇ f(t) dt plus correction terms involving Bernoulli numbers and derivatives of f at the endpoints, with a remainder expressible as an integral involving Bernoulli polynomials.

name: Summation of divergent series by Euler-Maclaurin
description: Using the Euler-Maclaurin formula to assign finite values to formally divergent sums by analytic continuation, yielding values for ζ(-n) in terms of Bernoulli numbers.

name: Asymptotic expansion of the gamma function
description: The Stirling series Γ(x) ~ √(2π) x^{x-1/2} e^{-x} (1 + Σₖ₌₁^∞ cₖ/x^k), an asymptotic expansion for x → +∞ with coefficients expressible via Bernoulli numbers.

name: Beta function
description: Defined as B(p,q) = ∫₀¹ t^{p-1}(1-t)^{q-1} dt for p, q > 0, related to the gamma function by B(p,q) = Γ(p)Γ(q)/Γ(p+q).

name: Digamma function
description: The logarithmic derivative ψ(x) = Γ'(x)/Γ(x) = (d/dx) log Γ(x), whose asymptotic expansion involves Bernoulli numbers: ψ(x) ~ log x - 1/(2x) - Σₖ₌₁^∞ B₂ₖ/(2k·x²ᵏ).

name: Abscissa of convergence
description: The infimum σ₀ of real numbers σ such that the Laplace integral ∫₀^∞ e^{-σt} f(t) dt converges, establishing a half-plane Re(s) > σ₀ of convergence.

name: Abscissa of absolute convergence
description: The infimum σₐ of real numbers σ such that ∫₀^∞ e^{-σt} |f(t)| dt converges, always satisfying σ₀ ≤ σₐ ≤ σ₀ + 1 for locally integrable f.

name: Laplace transform of derivatives
description: L{f'}(s) = sL{f}(s) - f(0⁺), and more generally L{f⁽ⁿ⁾}(s) = sⁿL{f}(s) - Σₖ₌₀ⁿ⁻¹ sⁿ⁻¹⁻ᵏ f⁽ᵏ⁾(0⁺), converting differential equations to algebraic equations.

name: Laplace transform of convolutions
description: L{f * g}(s) = L{f}(s) · L{g}(s), where (f * g)(t) = ∫₀ᵗ f(t-u) g(u) du, converting convolution to pointwise multiplication.

name: Inversion formula for Laplace transform
description: Under suitable conditions, f(t) = (1/2πi) ∫_{c-i∞}^{c+i∞} e^{st} L{f}(s) ds for c > σ₀, recovering f from its Laplace transform via a Bromwich contour integral.

name: Uniqueness theorem for Laplace transform
description: If L{f}(s) = L{g}(s) for all s in a half-plane and f, g are continuous, then f = g, establishing injectivity of the Laplace transform on continuous functions.

name: Application of Laplace transform to linear ODE
description: Converting a linear ODE with constant coefficients and initial conditions to an algebraic equation via Laplace transform, solving algebraically, then inverting to obtain the solution.
function_signature: (Linear ODE with initial conditions) → (Algebraic equation → Solution via inversion)

name: Valued field
description: A field K equipped with an absolute value |·|: K → R₊ satisfying |xy| = |x||y| and the triangle inequality, inducing a metric topology on K.

name: Neighborhood of zero (fundamental system)
description: In a TVS, the topology is entirely determined by a fundamental system of neighborhoods of the origin, which must be absorbing, balanced sets; translations then give the full topology.

name: Absorbing set
description: A subset A of a vector space E such that for every x ∈ E there exists λ₀ > 0 with x ∈ λA for all |λ| ≥ λ₀.

name: Balanced set
description: A subset B of a vector space E such that λB ⊆ B for all scalars λ with |λ| ≤ 1.

name: Bounded set in a TVS
description: A subset B of a TVS E is bounded if for every neighborhood V of 0, there exists λ > 0 such that B ⊆ λV, equivalently if B is absorbed by every neighborhood of zero.

name: Metrizable TVS
description: A TVS whose topology is metrizable, which occurs if and only if it has a countable fundamental system of neighborhoods of zero, in which case it can be metrized by a translation-invariant metric.

name: Normable TVS
description: A TVS whose topology can be defined by a single norm, characterized by having a bounded convex neighborhood of zero.

name: Completeness of a TVS
description: A TVS is complete if every Cauchy net (or Cauchy filter) converges; a complete metrizable locally convex space is a Fréchet space.

name: Topological direct sum of TVS
description: A TVS E is a topological direct sum of subspaces E₁ and E₂ if the map (x₁, x₂) ↦ x₁ + x₂ is a topological isomorphism from E₁ × E₂ to E.

name: Quotient TVS
description: For a closed subspace F of a TVS E, the quotient E/F with the quotient topology is again a TVS, and E/F is Hausdorff if and only if F is closed.

name: Product of TVS
description: The Cartesian product Πᵢ Eᵢ of TVS equipped with the product topology is again a TVS, and it is locally convex (resp. complete) if each factor is.

name: Minkowski functional (gauge)
description: For a convex absorbing set C containing 0, the Minkowski functional is p_C(x) = inf{λ > 0 : x ∈ λC}, which is a sublinear function and a seminorm when C is balanced.

name: Strict separation theorem
description: If A is a closed convex set and B is a compact convex set in a locally convex space with A ∩ B = ∅, then there exists a continuous linear functional strictly separating them: sup_{a∈A} f(a) < inf_{b∈B} f(b).

name: Supporting hyperplane theorem
description: At every boundary point of a closed convex set in a locally convex space, there exists a closed hyperplane containing the point and having the convex set on one side.

name: Bipolar theorem
description: For a subset A of a locally convex space, the bipolar A°° equals the closed convex balanced hull of A.

name: Space of continuous linear maps L(E, F)
description: The vector space of all continuous linear maps from a TVS E to a TVS F, which can be given various topologies depending on the notion of convergence desired.

name: Topology of bounded convergence (strong topology on L(E,F))
description: The topology on L(E,F) of uniform convergence on bounded subsets of E, making L(E,F) into a locally convex space when F is locally convex.

name: Topology of pointwise convergence (weak topology on L(E,F))
description: The coarsest topology on L(E,F) making all evaluation maps u ↦ u(x) continuous, also called the simple topology.

name: Barrelled space
description: A locally convex space in which every barrel (closed, convex, balanced, absorbing set) is a neighborhood of zero; every Fréchet space and every Baire locally convex space is barrelled.

name: Barrel
description: A subset of a TVS that is closed, convex, balanced, and absorbing.

name: Weak-* topology σ(E', E)
description: The weak topology on the dual E' of a TVS E induced by the duality ⟨E', E⟩, under which E' is a locally convex space and E embeds canonically into (E')'.

name: Mackey topology τ(E, F)
description: The finest locally convex topology on E consistent with the duality ⟨E, F⟩, defined as the topology of uniform convergence on σ(F, E)-compact convex balanced subsets of F.

name: Semi-reflexive space
description: A locally convex space E is semi-reflexive if the canonical map J: E → E'' is surjective (algebraic isomorphism), without requiring it to be a homeomorphism.

name: Strong topology β(E', E)
description: The topology on E' of uniform convergence on all bounded subsets of E, making E' a locally convex space called the strong dual.

name: Grothendieck completion theorem
description: Every Hausdorff locally convex space has a completion that is unique up to topological isomorphism, constructed as a subspace of the algebraic dual of E' with the topology of uniform convergence on equicontinuous sets.

name: Transpose (adjoint) of a continuous linear map
description: For u: E → F continuous linear, the transpose ᵗu: F' → E' is defined by ⟨ᵗu(f), x⟩ = ⟨f, u(x)⟩, and ᵗu is continuous for the weak-* and strong topologies.

name: Weak compactness and completeness
description: In a complete locally convex space, a closed bounded set is weakly compact if and only if every bounded sequence has a weakly convergent subsequence.

name: Parallelogram law
description: In an inner product space, ‖x+y‖² + ‖x-y‖² = 2(‖x‖² + ‖y‖²), and a normed space satisfying this identity is an inner product space (Jordan-von Neumann theorem).

name: Orthogonality
description: Two elements x, y of an inner product space are orthogonal (x ⊥ y) if ⟨x,y⟩ = 0; a set S is orthogonal if its elements are pairwise orthogonal.

name: Orthogonal projection theorem
description: For every closed subspace M of a Hilbert space H, each x ∈ H has a unique decomposition x = m + m⊥ with m ∈ M and m⊥ ∈ M⊥, and m is the unique best approximation of x from M.

name: Orthonormal system
description: A family (eᵢ) in a Hilbert space such that ⟨eᵢ, eⱼ⟩ = δᵢⱼ (Kronecker delta), i.e., pairwise orthogonal unit vectors.

name: Normal operator
description: A bounded linear operator T on a Hilbert space satisfying T*T = TT*, implying the spectral theorem applies.

name: Direct sum of Hilbert spaces
description: The Hilbert space direct sum ⊕ᵢ Hᵢ consists of families (xᵢ) with xᵢ ∈ Hᵢ and Σᵢ ‖xᵢ‖² < ∞, equipped with the inner product ⟨(xᵢ),(yᵢ)⟩ = Σᵢ ⟨xᵢ,yᵢ⟩.

name: Young's inequality for products
description: For a, b >= 0 and conjugate exponents p, q (1/p + 1/q = 1): ab <= a^p/p + b^q/q, with equality iff a^p = b^q.

name: Conjugate exponents
description: A pair (p, q) with 1 <= p, q <= infinity satisfying 1/p + 1/q = 1, fundamental to Lp space duality and Holder's inequality.

name: Log-convexity of Lp norms (Riesz interpolation inequality)
description: For 1 <= p1 <= p <= p2 <= infinity, if f in Lp1 cap Lp2, then f in Lp and ||f||_p <= ||f||_{p1}^theta ||f||_{p2}^{1-theta} where 1/p = theta/p1 + (1-theta)/p2.

name: Bounded Radon measure
description: A Radon measure mu on X that extends to a continuous linear form on C_0(X), equivalently one with finite total variation |mu|(X) < infinity.

name: Support of a measure
description: The smallest closed set F such that mu(f) = 0 for every continuous function f with compact support contained in X \ F.

name: Total variation measure
description: For a complex Radon measure mu, the positive measure |mu| defined by |mu|(f) = sup{|mu(g)| : |g| <= f, g in K(X)} for f >= 0, making bounded measures a Banach space under ||mu|| = |mu|(X).

name: Vague topology on measures
description: The weak-* topology sigma(M(X), K(X)) on the space of Radon measures, where mu_n -> mu vaguely iff mu_n(f) -> mu(f) for all f in K(X).

name: Dirac measure
description: The measure delta_x defined by delta_x(f) = f(x) for a point x in X, the atomic probability measure concentrated at a single point.

name: Image measure (pushforward measure)
description: For a proper continuous map phi: X -> Y and a measure mu on X, the image measure phi_*(mu) on Y defined by phi_*(mu)(f) = mu(f o phi).

name: Regularity of Radon measures
description: Every Radon measure on a locally compact space is inner regular (approximable from below by compact sets) and outer regular (approximable from above by open sets) on sigma-finite measurable sets.

name: Upper integral
description: For a positive measure mu and a lower semicontinuous function f >= 0, defined as mu*(f) = sup{mu(g) : g in K(X), 0 <= g <= f}, extending integration beyond continuous functions.

name: Measurable function (Bourbaki, mu-measurable)
description: A function f: X -> R is mu-measurable if for every compact K and epsilon > 0, there exists compact K' subset K with mu(K \ K') < epsilon such that f|_{K'} is continuous (Lusin characterization).

name: Integrable function (Lebesgue integrable)
description: A measurable function f is mu-integrable if integral |f| dmu < infinity, where the integral is defined via the Daniell construction extending from continuous functions with compact support.

name: Negligible set (mu-null set)
description: A set N subset X is mu-negligible if mu*(chi_N) = 0, equivalently if it is contained in an open set of arbitrarily small measure.

name: Lp space (1 <= p < infinity)
description: The Banach space of equivalence classes of measurable functions f with integral |f|^p dmu < infinity, modulo equality a.e., with norm ||f||_p = (integral |f|^p dmu)^{1/p}.

name: L-infinity space
description: The Banach space of equivalence classes of essentially bounded measurable functions, with norm ||f||_infinity = ess sup |f| = inf{M : |f| <= M a.e.}.

name: Dense subspaces of Lp
description: For 1 <= p < infinity, the space K(X) of continuous functions with compact support is dense in Lp(mu), as is the space of simple functions.

name: Essential supremum
description: The essential supremum of a measurable function f is ess sup f = inf{M in R : f <= M a.e.}, the smallest a.e. upper bound.

name: Convergence in measure
description: A sequence (f_n) converges to f in measure if for every epsilon > 0, mu({x : |f_n(x) - f(x)| > epsilon}) -> 0; Lp convergence implies convergence in measure.

name: Product measure
description: For sigma-finite measures mu on X and nu on Y, the unique measure mu tensor nu on X x Y satisfying (mu tensor nu)(A x B) = mu(A) nu(B) for measurable rectangles.

name: Tonelli's theorem
description: If f is a non-negative measurable function on X x Y, then integral f d(mu tensor nu) = integral integral f(x,y) dmu(x) dnu(y), with iterated integrals equal without assuming integrability.

name: Change of variables formula (integration on Rn)
description: If phi: U -> V is a C1 diffeomorphism between open sets in Rn, then integral_V f(y) dy = integral_U f(phi(x)) |det J_phi(x)| dx for integrable f.

name: Bochner integral
description: The integral of a strongly measurable function f: X -> E (E a Banach space) with integral ||f|| dmu < infinity, defined as the limit of integrals of simple functions; f is Bochner integrable iff ||f|| is Lebesgue integrable.

name: Strongly measurable function
description: A function f: X -> E (E separable Banach space) is strongly measurable if it is the a.e. limit of a sequence of simple (measurable, finitely-valued) functions.

name: Vector-valued measure (vector measure)
description: A countably additive map mu: Sigma -> E from a sigma-algebra into a Banach space, generalizing scalar measures.

name: Radon-Nikodym derivative (density)
description: The a.e. unique measurable function dnu/dmu satisfying nu(A) = integral_A (dnu/dmu) dmu for all measurable sets A, existing when nu << mu and both are sigma-finite.

name: Left invariance of Haar measure
description: A measure mu on a topological group G is left-invariant if mu(gA) = mu(A) for all g in G and all measurable A, equivalently integral f(g^{-1}x) dmu(x) = integral f(x) dmu(x).

name: Right Haar measure
description: A right-invariant positive Radon measure on G, related to left Haar measure via the modular function: d mu_r(x) = Delta(x^{-1}) d mu_l(x).

name: Modular function
description: The continuous homomorphism Delta: G -> R_+* defined by mu(Ag) = Delta(g) mu(A) for left Haar measure mu, measuring the failure of left Haar measure to be right-invariant.

name: Unimodular group
description: A locally compact group whose modular function is identically 1, so left and right Haar measures coincide; includes all compact groups, abelian groups, and semisimple Lie groups.

name: Haar measure on compact groups
description: On a compact group, the Haar measure is both left- and right-invariant (unimodular) and can be normalized to a probability measure with mu(G) = 1.

name: Integration formula for quotient groups
description: If H is a closed subgroup of G with Haar measures mu_G, mu_H, and G/H admits an invariant measure, then integral_G f dmu_G = integral_{G/H} (integral_H f(xh) dmu_H(h)) dmu_{G/H}(xH).

name: Weil's formula (quotient integral formula)
description: A G-invariant measure on the quotient space G/H exists if and only if Delta_G|_H = Delta_H, and when it exists it is unique up to a positive scalar.

name: Convolution of measures
description: For bounded Radon measures mu and nu on a locally compact group G, the convolution (mu * nu)(f) = integral integral f(xy) dmu(x) dnu(y), making bounded measures a Banach algebra.

name: Convolution of functions on a group
description: For f, g in L1(G), the convolution (f * g)(x) = integral_G f(xy^{-1}) g(y) dmu(y) with respect to left Haar measure, making L1(G) a Banach algebra.

name: Approximate identity in L1(G)
description: A net (e_i) in L1(G) with integral e_i dmu = 1 and support shrinking to {e} such that e_i * f -> f in L1 norm for all f, replacing the absent unit element.

name: Character of a representation
description: The character of a finite-dimensional representation pi is the function chi_pi(g) = tr(pi(g)), a continuous class function that determines the representation up to equivalence.

name: Convolution algebra of measures M(G)
description: The Banach space of bounded Radon measures on G with convolution as multiplication and total variation as norm, forming a unital Banach algebra with unit delta_e.

name: Integrated representation
description: For a unitary representation pi of G on H, the integrated form pi~: L1(G) -> B(H) defined by pi~(f) = integral_G f(g) pi(g) dmu(g) is a non-degenerate *-representation of the group algebra.

name: Fourier transform on locally compact abelian groups
description: For f in L1(G), the Fourier transform f_hat(chi) = integral_G f(g) overline{chi(g)} dmu(g) for chi in G_hat, mapping L1(G) to C_0(G_hat) and satisfying (f * g)^ = f_hat g_hat.

name: Fourier inversion formula (LCA groups)
description: Under appropriate normalization of Haar measures, if f in L1(G) and f_hat in L1(G_hat), then f(g) = integral_{G_hat} f_hat(chi) chi(g) d mu_hat(chi) for a.e. g.

name: Tight measure
description: A Borel measure mu on a topological space X is tight if for every epsilon > 0, there exists a compact set K with mu(X \ K) < epsilon.

name: Weak convergence of measures (narrow convergence)
description: A sequence of measures mu_n converges weakly to mu if integral f dmu_n -> integral f dmu for all bounded continuous functions f.

name: Regular Borel measure
description: A Borel measure that is both inner regular (mu(A) = sup{mu(K) : K subset A compact}) and outer regular (mu(A) = inf{mu(U) : U supset A open}) on all measurable sets.

name: Inner regularity
description: A measure mu is inner regular on a measurable set A if mu(A) = sup{mu(K) : K subset A, K compact}.

name: Outer regularity
description: A measure mu is outer regular on a measurable set A if mu(A) = inf{mu(U) : A subset U, U open}.

name: Suslin space (analytic space)
description: A Hausdorff topological space that is the continuous image of a Polish space; every Borel subset of a Polish space is Suslin, and measures on Suslin spaces have strong regularity properties.

name: Choquet capacitability theorem
description: In a Suslin space, every analytic set is capacitable, meaning its outer measure equals the supremum of measures of compact subsets, extending inner regularity to analytic sets.

name: Daniell integral approach
function_signature: (Positive linear functional on lattice of functions) -> (Complete measure and integration theory)
description: Bourbaki's method of defining integration starting from a positive linear functional on a lattice of functions, then extending via upper integrals and completion, rather than from a measure on sets.

name: Approximation by continuous functions
function_signature: (Measurable or integrable function, epsilon > 0) -> (Continuous function with compact support within epsilon)
description: The systematic use of Urysohn's lemma and partitions of unity to approximate measurable or integrable functions by continuous functions with compact support.

name: Inductive limit topology
description: The finest locally convex topology on K(X) = union_K C(K) making all inclusion maps C(K) -> K(X) continuous, used in Bourbaki's definition of Radon measures.

name: Abel-Liouville formula (Wronskian formula)
description: The Wronskian of solutions of y' = A(t)y satisfies W(t) = W(t_0) exp(integral_{t_0}^t tr A(s) ds), showing it is either identically zero or never zero.

name: Pontryagin dual group
description: For a locally compact abelian group G, the dual group G_hat = Hom(G, T) is the group of continuous homomorphisms from G to the circle group T, equipped with the compact-open topology.

name: Spectral radius formula
description: For a bounded linear operator T on a Banach space, the spectral radius r(T) = lim ||T^n||^{1/n} = inf ||T^n||^{1/n}.

name: Resolvent of an operator
description: For lambda not in sigma(T), the resolvent R(lambda,T) = (lambda I - T)^{-1} is a bounded operator depending analytically on lambda, satisfying the resolvent identity R(lambda) - R(mu) = (mu - lambda)R(lambda)R(mu).

name: Pettis integral (weak integral)
description: A vector x in E is the Pettis integral of f: X -> E if <x, x'> = integral <f, x'> dmu for all x' in E'; weaker than Bochner, requiring only scalar measurability.

name: Convolution semigroup
description: A family (mu_t)_{t>=0} of probability measures on a locally compact group satisfying mu_s * mu_t = mu_{s+t} and mu_0 = delta_e, modeling diffusion and Markov processes on groups.

name: Lie algebra homomorphism
description: A linear map φ: g → h between Lie algebras satisfying φ([x,y]) = [φ(x),φ(y)] for all x,y in g.

name: Quotient Lie algebra
description: For an ideal a of g, the vector space g/a equipped with the bracket [x+a, y+a] = [x,y]+a, yielding a well-defined Lie algebra structure.

name: Center of a Lie algebra
description: The ideal z(g) = {x ∈ g : [x,y] = 0 for all y ∈ g}, consisting of elements that bracket trivially with all of g.

name: Derived subalgebra (commutator subalgebra)
description: The ideal [g,g] = D(g) spanned by all brackets [x,y], measuring the failure of g to be abelian.

name: Derived series
description: The descending sequence D⁰(g) = g, Dⁿ⁺¹(g) = [Dⁿ(g), Dⁿ(g)] obtained by iterating the derived subalgebra construction.

name: Radical of a Lie algebra
description: The unique maximal solvable ideal rad(g) of a finite-dimensional Lie algebra g, which contains every solvable ideal.

name: Simple Lie algebra
description: A non-abelian Lie algebra whose only ideals are 0 and itself, serving as the irreducible building blocks of semisimple Lie algebras.

name: Lie's theorem
description: If g is a solvable Lie algebra over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero and V is a finite-dimensional g-module, then there exists a common eigenvector for all elements of g acting on V.

name: Cartan's criterion for solvability
description: A finite-dimensional Lie algebra g over a field of characteristic zero is solvable if and only if B(x,y) = 0 for all x ∈ g and y ∈ [g,g], where B is the Killing form.

name: Cartan's criterion for semisimplicity
description: A finite-dimensional Lie algebra g over a field of characteristic zero is semisimple if and only if its Killing form is non-degenerate.

name: Levi decomposition
description: Every finite-dimensional Lie algebra g over a field of characteristic zero is a semidirect product g = rad(g) ⋊ s where s is a semisimple subalgebra (called a Levi factor), and any two Levi factors are conjugate.

name: Poincaré-Birkhoff-Witt theorem
description: If {x₁,...,xₙ} is an ordered basis of g, then the monomials x₁^{a₁}···xₙ^{aₙ} form a basis of U(g), proving the canonical map g → U(g) is injective.

name: Normalizer of a subalgebra
description: For a subalgebra h of g, the subalgebra N_g(h) = {x ∈ g : [x,h] ⊆ h}, the largest subalgebra of g in which h is an ideal.

name: Centralizer in a Lie algebra
description: For a subset S of g, the subalgebra C_g(S) = {x ∈ g : [x,s] = 0 for all s ∈ S}, consisting of elements commuting with all of S.

name: Semidirect product of Lie algebras
description: Given Lie algebras h and a with a representation ρ: h → der(a), the vector space h ⊕ a with bracket [(h₁,a₁),(h₂,a₂)] = ([h₁,h₂], [a₁,a₂]+ρ(h₁)a₂−ρ(h₂)a₁).

name: Derivation of a Lie algebra
description: A linear map D: g → g satisfying D([x,y]) = [D(x),y] + [x,D(y)], with inner derivations being those of the form ad(x).

name: Whitehead's lemma (first)
description: For a semisimple Lie algebra g over a field of characteristic zero and a finite-dimensional g-module V, every derivation from g to V is inner, i.e., H¹(g,V) = 0.

name: Whitehead's lemma (second)
description: For a semisimple Lie algebra g over characteristic zero and a finite-dimensional g-module V, every extension of g by V splits, i.e., H²(g,V) = 0.

name: Jordan decomposition in a Lie algebra
description: In a semisimple Lie algebra g over a perfect field, each element x has a unique decomposition x = xₛ + xₙ with xₛ semisimple, xₙ nilpotent, and [xₛ,xₙ] = 0, compatible with any faithful representation.

name: Invariant bilinear form
description: A bilinear form B on g satisfying B([x,y],z) = B(x,[y,z]) for all x,y,z ∈ g, with the Killing form being the canonical example.

name: Witt formula
description: The dimension of the degree-n homogeneous component of the free Lie algebra on q generators is (1/n)∑_{d|n} μ(d)q^{n/d}, where μ is the Möbius function.

name: Baker-Campbell-Hausdorff formula
description: For elements x,y in a complete filtered Lie algebra (or in a neighborhood of identity in a Lie group), log(eˣeʸ) = x + y + ½[x,y] + 1/12([x,[x,y]]+[y,[y,x]]) + ···, expressing the group product in terms of iterated Lie brackets.

name: Lie group homomorphism
description: A smooth group homomorphism between Lie groups, whose differential at the identity is a Lie algebra homomorphism.

name: Lie algebra of a Lie group
description: The tangent space at the identity g = T_eG equipped with the Lie bracket inherited from left-invariant vector fields, functorially associated to the Lie group G.

name: Lie subgroup
description: A subgroup H of a Lie group G that is an immersed submanifold (or, in the closed case, an embedded submanifold) carrying an induced Lie group structure.

name: Closed subgroup theorem (Cartan's theorem)
description: Every closed subgroup of a Lie group is an embedded Lie subgroup, i.e., it automatically inherits a smooth manifold structure making it a Lie group in the subspace topology.

name: Quotient of a Lie group
description: For a closed normal subgroup N of G, the quotient G/N carries a unique Lie group structure making the projection G → G/N a smooth surjective homomorphism with Lie algebra g/n.

name: Lie functor
description: The functor Lie: LieGrp → LieAlg sending each Lie group to its Lie algebra and each homomorphism to its differential at the identity, providing the algebraic linearization of group theory.

name: Integration of Lie algebra homomorphisms
description: The process of lifting a Lie algebra homomorphism g → h to a Lie group homomorphism G → H when G is simply connected, by using the exponential map and path-lifting.

name: Coxeter group
description: A group W with a presentation ⟨s₁,...,sₙ | (sᵢsⱼ)^{mᵢⱼ} = 1⟩ where mᵢᵢ = 1 and mᵢⱼ = mⱼᵢ ≥ 2 (or ∞), abstracting the structure of reflection groups.

name: Coxeter matrix
description: A symmetric matrix M = (mᵢⱼ) with mᵢᵢ = 1 and mᵢⱼ ∈ {2,3,...,∞} for i≠j, encoding the orders of products of pairs of generators in a Coxeter group.

name: Coxeter graph
description: A labeled graph with vertices indexed by generators of a Coxeter group, edges connecting pairs with mᵢⱼ ≥ 3, and edge labels mᵢⱼ when mᵢⱼ ≥ 4, encoding the Coxeter matrix.

name: Exchange property
description: In a Coxeter group, if ℓ(sw) < ℓ(w) for a simple reflection s, then there exists an index i such that sw = s₁···ŝᵢ···sₖ (omitting sᵢ) for any reduced expression w = s₁···sₖ.

name: Deletion property
description: In a Coxeter group, any non-reduced expression s₁···sₖ can be shortened by deleting an even number of factors to obtain a reduced expression for the same element.

name: Tits system (BN-pair)
description: A group G with subgroups B and N such that B ∩ N = T is normal in N, W = N/T is a Coxeter group with generators S, and the axioms BwB·BsB ⊆ BwsB ∪ BwB and sBs⁻¹ ⊄ B hold for all w ∈ W, s ∈ S.

name: Parabolic subgroup of a Coxeter group
description: For a subset J ⊆ S of simple reflections, the subgroup W_J generated by J, which is itself a Coxeter group with Coxeter matrix restricted to J.

name: Coxeter complex
description: The simplicial complex associated to a Coxeter group W whose simplices are cosets of parabolic subgroups of W, serving as the building block (apartment) of a Tits building.

name: Matsumoto's theorem
description: Any two reduced expressions for the same element of a Coxeter group are related by a sequence of braid relations sᵢsⱼsᵢ··· = sⱼsᵢsⱼ··· (mᵢⱼ factors each side), without requiring insertion/deletion.

name: Strong exchange property
description: In a Coxeter group, if ℓ(tw) < ℓ(w) for a reflection t (not necessarily simple), then t can replace one of the factors in any reduced expression for w.

name: Classification of finite Coxeter groups
description: The irreducible finite Coxeter groups are exactly the types Aₙ, Bₙ, Dₙ, E₆, E₇, E₈, F₄, G₂ (crystallographic, i.e., Weyl groups) together with H₃, H₄, and I₂(m) (non-crystallographic).

name: Coroot
description: For a root α, the coroot α∨ = 2α/⟨α,α⟩, such that the reflection s_α(β) = β − ⟨β,α∨⟩α, and the coroots form the dual root system.

name: Cartan matrix
description: The n×n integer matrix A = (aᵢⱼ) where aᵢⱼ = ⟨αᵢ,αⱼ∨⟩ for simple roots αᵢ,αⱼ, satisfying aᵢᵢ = 2, aᵢⱼ ≤ 0 for i≠j, and aᵢⱼ = 0 iff aⱼᵢ = 0, determining the root system up to isomorphism.

name: Classification of irreducible root systems
description: The connected Dynkin diagrams (equivalently irreducible root systems) are exactly Aₙ (n≥1), Bₙ (n≥2), Cₙ (n≥3), Dₙ (n≥4), E₆, E₇, E₈, F₄, and G₂.
